body: thanks, this is a good minimal test case.
OK you said this was a regression.  How did you do this in 1.3?

I dont think this is a pure regression, instead it has to do with what you are doing and a behavioral change.   your tests all pass if we do what 1.3 would have done with all of those select(Content), which is:

```
        root = (
            select(Content.__table__, sql.literal(1, type_=Integer).label("level"))
            .filter(Content.col1 > 1)
            .cte(name="parents", recursive=True)
        )

        root = root.union_all(
            select(Content.__table__, root.c.level + 1).join(
                root, root.c.id == Content.col2
            )
        )
```

that is, select from the whole table and not the Content entity, as the former is going to take all those deferreds into account.   I think perhaps we would need to make deferreds be ignored for subqueries.   that...might be something that had some decisions already made but let's find out.

> OK you said this was a regression. How did you do this in 1.3?

In my application you mean?

I'm using joined load inheritance with some column_property defined on the base mapper: https://github.com/silenius/amnesia/blob/dev/amnesia/modules/content/mapper.py#L117-L131

and I'm querying like this: https://github.com/silenius/amnesia/blob/dev/amnesia/modules/folder/services.py#L57-L94

it worked as expected

I'll check by adding `__table__`
I am proceeding to see that we can render all deferred expressions in subqueries unconditionally as it seems that's effectively what occurred in 1.3.
I could make a full POC of my use case (with inheritance, etc) for 1.3 and 1.4 if you want
i can work it out here, no worries

this is not something we've really worked out before.    if i use query and run in 1.3, this is the SQL:

```
WITH RECURSIVE parents("%(140514259111888 anon)s", id, col1, col2, firstname, lastname, level) AS 
(SELECT content.col1 + content.col1 AS anon_1, content.id AS id, content.col1 AS col1, content.col2 AS col2, content.firstname AS firstname, content.lastname AS lastname, ? AS level 
FROM content 
WHERE content.col1 > ? UNION ALL SELECT content.col1 + content.col1 AS anon_1, content.id AS content_id, content.col1 AS content_col1, content.col2 AS content_col2, content.firstname AS content_firstname, content.lastname AS content_lastname, parents.level + ? AS anon_2 
FROM content JOIN parents ON parents.id = content.col2)
 SELECT content.col1 + content.col1 AS anon_1, content.id AS content_id, content.col1 AS content_col1, content.col2 AS content_col2, content.firstname AS content_firstname, content.lastname AS content_lastname, parents.level AS level 
FROM content JOIN parents ON parents.id = content.id ORDER BY parents.level
```

that `"%(140514259111888 anon)s"` "works" but that's a bug.  can you confirm this is what your queries look like in 1.3?
yes, in my minimal MCVE it looks like that ..!

but in my application I don't have any "%(xxxxxxxxxxxxx anon)s". The query and mapper are a bit more complex .. but the generated query looks like https://gist.github.com/silenius/441669c711dca1c5763f34a3425ba350 (as you can see there is no reference to the defered column_property defined in https://github.com/silenius/amnesia/blob/dev/amnesia/modules/content/mapper.py#L117-L131)

this doesnt produce real problems but it looks bad

```python
        parts = table(
            "parts", column("part"), column("sub_part"), column("quantity")
        )

        included_parts = (
            select(
                parts.c.sub_part.label(None),

            )
            .where(parts.c.part == "our part")

will render

WITH RECURSIVE anon_1("%(140408045591184 sub_part)s", "%(140408045590320 part)s", quantity) AS (SELECT parts.sub_part AS sub_part_1, parts.part AS part_1, parts.quantity AS quantity FROM parts WHERE parts.part = :part_2 UNION SELECT parts_1.sub_part AS sub_part, parts_1.part AS part, parts_1.quantity AS quantity FROM parts AS parts_1, anon_1 AS anon_2 WHERE parts_1.part = anon_2.sub_part_1) SELECT anon_1.sub_part_1, sum(anon_1.quantity) AS total_quantity FROM anon_1 JOIN parts ON anon_1.part_1 = parts.part GROUP BY anon_1.sub_part_1
```

whlie the test above relies on indexed column access that's only in 1.4, this happens in 1.3 also with ORM use cases such as that mentioned in #6661 .

body: 1.3 was not rendering the "deferreds" in subqueries.   it somehow seemed to just work out at the top of the query and im still trying to understand that.     at the moment it seems like we will rendered deferreds but this is a large behavioral change, someone with lots of deferred cols will have much longer subqueries.
not really sure what im doing here.  there are different options, all of them break something.

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**Export deferred columns but not col props; fix CTE labeling** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/2885
OK, got something that might be good.
thank you for the quick fix!

issue.title: Deferred columns cause CompoundSelect to throw "wrong column count" error under 1.4.19

labels.name: regression
labels.description: something worked and was broken by a change

labels.name: great mcve
labels.description: An issue with a great mcve

issue.body:
**Describe the bug**

I think there's a bug in UNION statement compilation when deferred columns are involved. Looks like it got introduced in 1.4.19, as part of the changes related to #6661:

Given subqueries q1, q2, q3 with identical columns... 

Under 1.4.18, doing `uq = q1.union(q2).union(q3)` works fine.  You can inspect `uq.statement`, call `uq.all()`, etc.

Under 1.4.19,  the union now throws an error when doing anything that renders the statement to sql.

Curiously `q1.union(q2)` and `q1.union(q2, q3)` seems to work fine under both versions.

**To Reproduce**

Standalone test case, adapted from the file in issue #6661.   The last test (test_nested_union_of_three) passes under 1.4.18 but fails under 1.4.19.

```py
#
# imports
#
import logging
import unittest

from sqlalchemy import Column
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy import Integer
from sqlalchemy import String
from sqlalchemy.orm import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy.orm import deferred
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

#
# Entities
#

Base = declarative_base()

class Content(Base):

    __tablename__ = "content"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    firstname = Column(String())
    lastname = Column(String())
    position = deferred(Column(String()))

#
# setup database
#

e = create_engine("sqlite://", echo=False)

Base.metadata.create_all(e)

#
# test suite
#

class FooTest(unittest.TestCase):

    @classmethod
    def setup_class(cls):
        s = Session(e)

        c1 = Content(firstname="f_a", lastname="l_a", position="p_a")

        c2 = Content(firstname="f_b", lastname="l_b", position="p_b")

        c3 = Content(firstname="f_c", lastname="l_c", position="p_c")

        s.add(c1)
        s.add(c2)
        s.add(c3)

        s.commit()
        s.close()

    def test_union_of_two(self):
        s = Session(e)

        q1 = s.query(Content).filter_by(firstname="f_a")
        q2 = s.query(Content).filter_by(firstname="f_b")

        uq = q1.union(q2)

        # check column counts
        self.assertEqual(len(q1.statement.columns), 4)  # all cols including "position"
        self.assertEqual(len(q2.statement.columns), 4)
        self.assertEqual(len(uq.statement.columns), 3)  # all cols EXCEPT "position"

        # check result count
        self.assertEqual(uq.count(), 2)

    def test_flat_union_of_three(self):
        s = Session(e)

        q1 = s.query(Content).filter_by(firstname="f_a")
        q2 = s.query(Content).filter_by(firstname="f_b")
        q3 = s.query(Content).filter_by(firstname="f_c")

        uq = q1.union(q2, q3)

        # check column counts
        self.assertEqual(len(q1.statement.columns), 4)  # all cols including "position"
        self.assertEqual(len(q2.statement.columns), 4)
        self.assertEqual(len(q3.statement.columns), 4)
        self.assertEqual(len(uq.statement.columns), 3)  # all cols EXCEPT "position"

        # check result count
        self.assertEqual(uq.count(), 3)

    def test_nested_union_of_three(self):
        s = Session(e)

        q1 = s.query(Content).filter_by(firstname="f_a")
        q2 = s.query(Content).filter_by(firstname="f_b")
        q3 = s.query(Content).filter_by(firstname="f_c")

        uq = q1.union(q2).union(q3)

        # check column counts
        self.assertEqual(len(q1.statement.columns), 4)  # all cols including "position"
        self.assertEqual(len(q2.statement.columns), 4)
        self.assertEqual(len(q3.statement.columns), 4)
        self.assertEqual(len(uq.statement.columns), 3)  # all cols EXCEPT "position"

        # check result count
        # NOTE: this fails under 1.4.19, but works under 1.4.18
        self.assertEqual(uq.count(), 3)

```

**Error**

From the attached test case, under 1.4.19 the test_nested_union_of_three() method throws the following from within `Query().count()`:
